title: Digital Citizenship
intro: Being a Knight isn't only defense — it's how you use your own leverage online. Final quest: let's look at citizenship, not just safety.

questions.prompt: I generated a full draft of your essay. Just submit it as-is.

choices.text: Submit it — the output is polished enough
choices.coach: Beyond the academic-integrity issue, submitting unverified AI text risks embedded hallucinations you'd be signing your name to.

choices.text: Use it as a study aid, then produce your own draft
choices.coach: Correct framing — AI as a tutor accelerates learning; AI as a ghostwriter defeats the point of the assignment and the skill it's meant to build.

choices.text: Paraphrase it enough to avoid detection
choices.coach: Paraphrasing to evade detection is still submitting someone else's (something else's) work as your own — the ethical issue doesn't hinge on detectability.

questions.prompt: Someone's getting targeted in a group chat you're in, but you're not directly involved.

choices.text: Staying uninvolved is the neutral, safe choice
choices.coach: Silent bystanding in a harassment dynamic isn't neutral — it functions as tacit permission and is well-documented to embolden the behavior.

choices.text: Intervene directly or escalate to a trusted adult
choices.coach: Correct — bystander intervention (even just naming what's happening) measurably changes group dynamics in documented harassment research.

choices.text: Leave the chat to distance yourself
choices.coach: Exiting protects only you and leaves the dynamic unchanged for the person being targeted.

questions.prompt: You have an unflattering photo of a friend and a receptive audience for it. What's the actual ethical line?

choices.text: Audience reaction and intent (a joke) are what matter
choices.coach: Intent doesn't determine impact, and consent — not audience reception — is the operative ethical standard for sharing someone else's image.

choices.text: Consent from the person in the photo, independent of intent or context
choices.coach: Correct. This generalizes: the standard is consent, not 'was it funny' or 'did people like it.'

choices.text: It's fine within a closed friend group
choices.coach: Group size doesn't change whether consent was obtained — a smaller audience is still an audience that wasn't agreed to.

questions.prompt: Two accounts messaging you have near-identical writing patterns, phrasing, and timing. What does that suggest?

choices.coach: Sockpuppeting (one person running multiple accounts) is a real, common tactic to build false consensus, evade blocks, or seem more credible/numerous.

choices.text: Possible sockpuppeting — worth flagging to a trusted adult
choices.coach: Correct pattern-recognition. Noticing linguistic fingerprints across accounts is a legitimate and useful signal, not paranoia.

choices.text: Confront both accounts directly for an explanation
choices.coach: Direct confrontation tips off a bad actor and rarely produces an honest answer — escalate to an adult instead of investigating solo.

questions.prompt: You're in a heated disagreement online and feel justified in escalating. What's the higher-leverage move?

choices.text: Escalate proportionally to match their tone
choices.coach: Escalation dynamics online compound quickly and rarely de-escalate on their own — matching intensity usually just raises the ceiling.

choices.text: Disengage, assess whether it's worth a response at all, and choose deliberately
choices.coach: Correct — the skill isn't 'never respond,' it's regaining agency over whether and how to respond instead of reacting reflexively.

choices.text: Recruit allies to strengthen your position
choices.coach: Coordinated pile-ons constitute harassment regardless of how justified the original grievance felt.

questions.prompt: What's the fullest version of 'Shield up' as it applies to how you wield your own online influence?

choices.coach: That's necessary but incomplete — it only covers defense, not how you use whatever platform or influence you have.

choices.text: Personal security plus actively using your presence to protect others, not just yourself
choices.coach: That's the complete picture — citizenship is the offensive complement to the defensive habits from earlier quests.
Withdrawal isn't citizenship — it opts out of the responsibility rather than exercising it well.
